articles.title: Your library isn't in the training data: making AI agents use it well
articles.excerpt: A model that doesn't know your library doesn't fail by doing nothing. It fails by confidently writing code for a library it does know. Ask an AI agent to write a React component with Jest tests and it…
articles.body: A model that doesn't know your library doesn't fail by doing nothing. It fails by confidently writing code for a library it does know. Ask an AI agent to write a React component with Jest tests and it'll do a decent job. There are millions of examples of both in its training data. Now ask it to use something it has never seen: your company's internal API client; your design system; a niche open source library; a new major version that changed everything. You'll get code that looks right, compiles in the agent's head, and is wrong in small, confident ways. The agent isn't guessing at random. It fills every gap with the closest thing it knows. An option name from a similar library. An import from the popular alternative. A return shape it assumed.

articles.body: Founders treat the demo-day cut like a compressed deck: title, problem, solution, market, ask—spoken over the same bullets the judges already have in PDF. That version gets watched at 1.5x and forgotten. The clip that sticks is the one that shows why you exist in under ninety seconds, then points people somewhere they can dig deeper. Here is a structure that works when the room is tired and the next founder is already lining up. Open on the moment of pain, not the company name Skip the logo sting. Start on the concrete failure: the founder who spent three nights rebuilding the same investor intro, the ops lead reconciling three tools by hand every Monday, the recruiter whose LinkedIn pitch gets ignored by senior engineers. Name the person and the friction.

articles.body: Top 20 Nikto Commands Every Security Professional Should Know Nikto is an open-source web server scanner that performs comprehensive tests against web servers for dangerous files, outdated software, misconfigurations, and other security issues . Written in Perl and built on LibWhisker2, Nikto supports SSL, proxies, host authentication, and attack encoding . Unlike application scanners such as Wapiti, Nikto focuses specifically on server-level reconnaissance and known dangerous paths rather than crawling application logic . This third entry in our series covers the twenty most practical Nikto commands, complete with explanations of when and why to use each one. 1. Basic Scan Against a Target nikto -h http://example.com The -h flag specifies the target host or URL.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 13, 1773: Astronomer Charles Messier discovers the Whirlpool Galaxy before we ever knew it was a galaxy
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 13, 1773, a French astronomer named Charles Messier discovered the "Whirlpool Galaxy," also known as Messier 51, or M51. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 13, 1773, a French astronomer named Charles Messier discovered the " Whirlpool Galaxy , " also known as Messier 51, or M51. Charles Messier was scanning the sky for objects that could confuse comet hunters when he catalogued the galaxy as M51. However, Messier wasn't able to see the spiral structure, and he didn't identify it as a galaxy. Seventy-two years later, another astronomer named William Parsons saw the whirlpool shape, but he thought it was a spiral nebula. Eventually, Edwin Hubble found out that M51 and other features like it were actually galaxies. Spiral galaxy M51 (NGC 5194), The Whirlpool Galaxy, displays its long arms which consist of stars and gas laced with dust arranged in long lanes, in this view from the Hubble Space Telescope.

articles.body: A flaw in Docker Hub, the registry where container images are published and downloaded, let one user push, pull, or delete images as another user. Docker fixed the flaw on September 30 and says it found no evidence that anyone exploited it. The flaw was in the feature that converts a personal account into an organization, Docker said in a security advisory on October 12.

articles.title: Earth's poles shifted surprisingly fast during the age of dinosaurs, ancient sea levels reveal
articles.excerpt: The location of Earth's geographic poles has changed several times over the past 320 million years in a process known as true polar wander.
articles.body: The location of Earth's geographic poles has changed several times over the past 320 million years in a process known as true polar wander, according to measurements of ancient flooding brought about by sea level changes resulting from our planet's crust shifting relative to Earth's spin axis. Such a shift can affect climate, both on local scales and globally, as regions that were by the poles find themselves moving down to lower latitudes and vice versa. This can then affect atmospheric circulation patterns, which affect climate across the world. The changes would have affected the environments in which life developed and evolved, from the age of the dinosaurs through to some of our oldest primate ancestors.
